page.text:
The natural numbers are the numbers of counting: zero, one, two, and so
on without end. This chapter builds them from the ground already laid.
First they are characterized abstractly by the Peano axioms -- a starting
point, a successor operation, and the principle of induction -- and then
a concrete set of naturals is assembled from the sets of the earlier
chapter, with addition defined by recursion.
